Soojin —

Thanks for the summary and the attachments. Quick answers from the commercial side:

- Pricing: For a 12-month 16-slot commit we should propose a blended committed rate with a burst credit bucket. My recommendation: 12-month reserve at $X/slot-month + pre-purchased burst credits (sized to 20% of monthly baseline) with overage billed at a higher unit price. The table in the Drive has two scenarios (conservative and aggressive).
- Credits vs hard reservation: credits give them flexibility and soften procurement approval; hard reservation gives clearer revenue and easier capacity booking. If procurement pushes for guaranteed latency we should bias toward a hybrid: committed baseline + committed burst tranche (e.g., +10 slots guaranteed) + additional on-demand credits.

Also flagged the contract for a standard SLA with a fallback clause: if burst cannot be guaranteed, we include automatic fallback to a quantized model variant and a 10% credit for impacted calls. That will vary by workload; Ben, is that okay from a finance recognition perspective?

— Laura

Finance/FinOps view and risk scenarios:

1) Pool booking: For a 16-slot 12-month commit starting Aug 1, we should earmark capacity now in planning (Q3 procurement risk: 10–12 week lead time for dedicated hardware alignment). If we treat this as a reserved commit for revenue recognition, we need a signed MSA before Aug 1 or push start date to when the purchase order is received.

2) Margins & credits: burst-credit model works for procurement but increases unit volatility. Recommend a conservative credit bucket equivalent to ~25% of expected burst consumption for first 3 months, then re-evaluate via telemetry. That reduces surprise with a small buffer.

3) Fallback quantization: good idea for SLA language; however, we must include a clear performance delta doc. Ops: can we pre-compile quantized variants and have them staged? Logan?

4) Accounting note: any large one-off onboarding professional services (migration) should be itemized separately to avoid revenue deferral complexity.

I'll draft the finance appendix and upload to Drive.

Soojin / team —

Infra ops notes:

- Lead time: For guaranteed reserved A100-equivalent slots we should plan a 10–12 week provisioning cadence if we need capacity isolation in us-west. That matches Ben's note; August 1 start is tight but feasible if procurement signs by May 3 (gives us runway for procurement -> hardware allocation -> staging).
- Burst architecture: we can support burst via two mechanisms: (a) pre-warmed burst pool (hot spare slots) that we assign to the customer when needed (fastest, costs margin), or (b) cross-tenant burst from a shared on-demand pool with QoS gating per tier (slower under pressure). Pre-warmed burst (+10 guaranteed) plus credits for additional on-demand spikes is the fastest from a latency SLO standpoint.
- Pre-compile: we can stage quantized variants and keep them in cache; the initial build will take ~3 business days per model variant. Recommend we include an explicit step in the MAP to pre-compile and stage the quantized model (owner: Infra).
- Risks: if there is a simultaneous high-burst across multiple large deals in Aug, shared pool contention could cause p95 to slip. We need a contingency in the MAP (fallback order and temporary regional spill to us-east with IN-approval).

I will add the runbook snippet to the Drive.

— Logan
